The output current is about 6.4× the 20 µA target (127.6 µA measured, a 538% error). That points to a mirror-ratio fault in the PMOS pair M3/M4. M3 (diode-connected, W=21.41 µm, L=1.005 µm) and M4 (W=142.4 µm, same L) have a W ratio of 142.4/21.41 ≈ 6.65, which accounts for the measured error. The NMOS pair M1/M2 is matched (both 13.75/4.155), so the ratio fault is in the PMOS pair. M4 is the more likely corrupted element because the mismatch is a wrong width on the output device. M3 being undersized would produce the same ratio, so it ranks second.

```json
{"ranking": ["M4", "M3", "M2"], "fault": "M4 width corrupted to 142.4 um (about 6.65x the reference M3 width of 21.41 um), giving a PMOS mirror ratio of about 6.65 instead of 1. Restoring M4 W to about 21.41 um should bring iout back to about 20 uA."}
```
